reading-text-files.label: Reading Text Files
reading-text-files.summary: Open existing text files with `with open(..., "r")`, read a whole file with `.read()` or process it one line at a time, and use relative paths for files inside the workspace.

sketch0.title: Open and read a whole text file

sc-open-read.title: Open a nested file for reading
sc-open-read.prompt: Which line safely opens `data/story.txt` for reading and gives the open file the name `file`?
sc-open-read.hint: Use a `with` block, the relative path, and read mode `r`.

help.concept: `with open(path, "r") as file:` opens an existing text file for reading and closes it automatically when the block ends.
help.hint_1: The relative path keeps the folder before the file name: `data/story.txt`.

sc-read-all.title: What .read() returns
sc-read-all.prompt: What does `file.read()` give you when `file` is an open text file?
sc-read-all.hint: Think about reading the complete contents at once.

help.concept: For a text file, `.read()` returns the remaining file contents as one string.
help.hint_1: It does not return one number per line.
help.hint_2: Choose the option describing one string containing the file text.

options.a: One string containing the remaining text
options.d: The number of lines in the file

sc-line-loop.title: Read one line at a time
sc-line-loop.prompt: Which pattern processes an open text file one line at a time?
sc-line-loop.hint: An open file can be used directly in a `for` loop.

help.concept: `for line in file:` gives the loop one line from the open file at a time.
help.hint_1: You do not need `.read()` when you want to iterate through the file directly.
help.hint_2: Look for the `for line in file:` pattern.

sc-with-cleanup.title: Why use with open
sc-with-cleanup.prompt: What happens to the file when execution leaves a `with open(...) as file:` block?
sc-with-cleanup.hint: The `with` statement manages the file resource for you.

help.concept: The `with` statement closes the file automatically when the block ends, even though you did not call `file.close()` yourself.
help.hint_1: The file is not deleted or rewritten.
help.hint_2: The managed file is closed after the block.

options.c: Python changes the file to write mode
options.d: Python keeps the file open forever

read-whole-file.title: Open and read a whole text file
read-whole-file.bodyMarkdown:
Programs often need text that already exists in a file. To read an existing text file, use a managed `with open(...)` block.

```python
with open("notes.txt", "r") as file:
    text = file.read()

print(text)
```

Here:

- `"notes.txt"` is the file path.
- `"r"` means **read mode**.
- `as file` gives the open file a variable name.
- `file.read()` returns the remaining text as one string.
- when the `with` block ends, Python closes the file automatically.

Use `.read()` when you want the file's contents as one complete string.

iterate-lines.title: Process a file one line at a time
iterate-lines.bodyMarkdown:
You do not have to read the whole file into one string. An open text file can be used directly in a `for` loop.

If `colors.txt` contains:

```text
red
blue
green
```

you can process each stored line separately:

```python
with open("colors.txt", "r") as file:
    for line in file:
        color = line.strip()
        print(color.upper())
```

`for line in file:` gives the loop one line at a time. `line.strip()` removes the newline and surrounding whitespace before the program uses that line.

relative-path.title: Read a file from a relative path
relative-path.bodyMarkdown:
A file can live inside a folder in the workspace. Write the folder and file name together as a **relative path**.

For this workspace:

```text
main.py
data/
  team.txt
```

`main.py` can read the nested text file like this:

```python
with open("data/team.txt", "r") as file:
    team = file.read().strip()

print(team)
```

The path `data/team.txt` means "the file `team.txt` inside the `data` folder." After `.read()` returns the text, you can store and process that string using string operations you already know.
